blockingFindings.finding: The three EP-derived proof commitments are carried, never derived. A valid-looking arbitrary digest, a same-cardinality swap between universeCommitment and outcomeSetCommitment, and a same-shape substitution of one for the other all pass the entire semantic and executable layer without a single check firing. They survive only because acceptedGolden is compared byte-for-byte to evidence.v7.json, which is provenance, not recomputation. The structural cause is that these three values occur only inside SemanticEvidenceV1, and check-evidence-v8.py never re-encodes SemanticEvidenceV1 under the canonical grammar; it consumes acceptedGolden.semanticEvidenceHex as given bytes. The predecessor checker check-evidence-v4.py binds all three to bundle.requiredUniverse.universeCommitment and bundle.verdictProof.{outcomeSetCommitment,derivationCommitment} at its lines 173-176 and 227-230, and check-evidence-v5/v6/v7 inherit that binding by importing it. check-evidence-v8.py neither pins nor imports check-evidence-v4.py, so the recomputation obligation is dropped at v8.

residuals.note: acceptedGolden, canonicalWireGrammar, runSubstitutionGoldens and d9Mapping are protected by byte equality to evidence.v7.json plus four hard-coded digest literals. check-evidence-v8.py performs zero wire re-encoding of its own. Thirteen of my mutations were caught solely by unlisted-predecessor-surface equality. Any surface a future successor moves into changedRootKeys instantly loses its only protection. Semantic obligations should not be carried by an exclusion list.

The bound changed roots are compared to constants embedded in the checker source (API_CONTRACT, DURABLE_RECOVERY_CONTRACT, SERIALIZED_CUSTODY_CONTRACT and peers) or to predecessor values with author-chosen string replacements. canonicalWireGrammar.records.RawProofInventoryV1.items reads 'blob(concat(sorted blob(0x8b, complete item bytes)))', which literally implies sorting the length-prefixed wrappers, while the shipped bytes and recordRules.sets sort the complete item record bytes. The two orders differ for this data. My first independent decoder rejected the shipped bytes until recordRules.sets resolved the ambiguity. An implementer reading only the per-record rule would produce a different EvidenceDigest and RunId.

The protected canonicalWireGrammar still names RT11 in RawProofInventoryV1.equalityRule and EP6 in several field types, while the consumed dependencies are EP8 and RT13. The stale-generation regex forbids EP7/RT12/VERSIONING v6/v7 but permits EP6/RT11, so the predecessor-generation labels survive inside the identity-protected surface. This is a weaker instance of the EV7-PF-08 fork.

EV7-PF-R01 (RT13 resolve-and-pin/availability/lease/fencing authority) appears materially addressed by the serializedCustodyContract and the reducer join, but I did not independently reimplement the 23-object acquire/retry/release, pending-expiry, crash-gap repin or contention probes. Carried forward as unverified-by-this-review.
